title: Coalescence anomaly deep-dive and fairness tuning notes
description: Working notes from an investigation into an intermittent latency anomaly we saw in continuous coalescing mode: small requests (<=32 tokens) occasionally hit long tail latencies while overall throughput looked healthy. Focus is on root causes around aggregation thresholds, eviction behavior, and fairness weight scheduling.
environment: staging-gpu-pool-v3; runtime=redwood-serving-1.8; torch=2.1; nv-driver=535; kernel-tunable-batcher=on; KV-cache=enabled
key_findings: Observed two distinct failure modes: (A) head-of-line blocking when a long request enters a growing coalesced batch, and (B) starvation of very small requests caused by minimum-batch-formation timer being too aggressive under bursty arrival patterns.

Microaggregation threshold set to 8ms creates an effective 'sticky' batch boundary; small requests arriving just after flush get delayed until next flush — p95 for <=32-token requests spiked by ~420ms in replay traces.
KV-cache prefill during batch formation increases variance: batches that included a cache-miss triggered extra work and delayed flush for subsequent queued requests, amplifying tail.
Introducing small randomized jitter to batch-timeout reduced correlated flush alignment and dropped observed p95 by ~18% in synthetic bursts.

Current fairness credit allocator overly favors throughput-class jobs; when throughput targets are hit, small interactive requests accumulate debt but are not prioritized quickly enough, leading to tails.
CPU-side scheduling (serialize kernel launches for mixed-length batches) contributes measurable overhead (~0.6ms per mixed batch) which is non-trivial for small-request latency budgets.
raw_measurements_summary: Baseline (continuous coalescer: min_wait=8ms, max_batch=64): p50(<=32t)=12ms, p90=48ms, p95=210ms, p99=780ms. After jitter+light-fairness tweak: p50=11ms, p90=42ms, p95=170ms, p99=560ms. Throughput difference negligible (<1.5% drop) on synthetic-high-mix. Mixed-batch CPU-scheduling overhead measured with perf traces: median 0.58ms, tail 3.2ms on coalesced batches containing both short+long requests.
actions_proposed: Experiment A: increase min_wait to 12ms but add randomized jitter +/-3ms to decorrelate flushes
Experiment B: implement a two-class coalescer window (interactive vs bulk) with soft headroom that forces a flush if interactive requests wait >30ms
Implement fairness-credit-burner: when interactive debt > threshold, preempt next batch formation and form a short batch (<=8 reqs) immediately
Add KV-cache-aware batch scoring: if a candidate batch contains >1 cache-miss, prioritize early flush to avoid cascading work
Add microbench harness to reproduce mixed-batch kernel serialization overhead and run native profiling on 1-2 GPU machines
